symbols.name: looksLikeAuthority
symbols.sig: export function looksLikeAuthority(text: string): boolean
doc: I call the bracketed text an authority only when it names who approves ("Head of P&A", "Concerned Functional Director", "CGM", "Chief Executive"), not when it is a note ("Mandatory", "Phase-1 Enrolment").

symbols.name: bracketIsAmount
symbols.sig: export function bracketIsAmount(text: string): boolean
doc: I treat a bracket as money when it holds an amount ("officer Rs - 250/- and employees/CW-Rs- 100/-", "Officers: Rs.500/-"): that is the penalty or the rate itself, never a note and never an approver, and the word "officer" in it does not make it one.

symbols.name: splitValueBracket
symbols.sig: export function splitValueBracket(trimmed: string): { rate: string; bracket: string; condition: string } | null
symbols.returns: { rate: string; bracket: string; condition: string } | null
doc: Splits a cell of the "value (bracket) [condition]" shape, or returns null when it is not that shape. I do not split a bracket glued to the word before it ("Section no: 5(Xii)" is a clause reference, one thing), nor a bracket that holds money: it stays inside the value, because the penalty is the answer, not a footnote.

a long account number (16 digits) keeps every digit
an 18-digit number keeps every digit too (a JavaScript number would lose the last ones)
an account number the model wrote with commas comes out unbroken
a shorter number under an identifier heading is unbroken as well
a wage under a money heading is still grouped
a year is still a year
col 0 contains bullet pulse
col 0 contains text
auth cell contains bold rate
auth cell contains authority badge
auth cell contains authority chip styling
a condition cell still draws the bold rate and the authority chip
a condition cell shows the condition as a note, without the brackets
not applicable cell has muted pill
not applicable cell has slate bg
not applicable cell text
compound not app cell has muted pill
compound not app cell has slate bg
compound not app cell text
admin auth cell rate
admin auth cell authority
abbr detects HRR
abbr detects P&A
abbr detects M&HS
abbr does not falsely include OPD
RFID is listed once
a made-up pairing is not picked up
an abbreviation is matched only in capitals: the words 'ed' and 'ta' are not ED and TA
an approver is an authority
'Mandatory' and 'Phase-1 Enrolment' are notes, not authorities
a note in brackets is drawn as a note, with no approver chip
money in a bracket is an amount, not an approver, although it says 'officer'
an approver or a note is not an amount
the penalty amounts stay in the value, with no approver chip, and the condition is the note
a second penalty row is drawn the same way as the first
a clause reference glued to its word is not split into a value and a note
a bracket that only finishes the phrase (an abbreviation after '&') is part of the sentence, not a note
a note after a finished value is still split
a sentence-long cell with a time in brackets stays one plain line (no bold lead, no detached note)
a title with its function in brackets is one designation, not a value with a footnote
a rate with an approver is still split
the chart and the table each show a Source row (2) with the circular's label
the Sources strip shows the circular's name next to its label, not cut to one line
a timeline shows no 'Metric:' tag
SSP is Salem Steel Plant, also in 'SSP gift' (the Kaushal Award circular: 'a Salem Steel made product', 'SSP items procured by MM through IPT')
DSP is shown when a reply says 'DSP Intranet' or 'DSP,' but not for the word inside another word
these are matched in capitals only: the ordinary words 'race', 'smart' and 'sd' are not abbreviations
its initials do spell DARPAN (filler 'by' skipped)
'Inc.' in a company name is not INC (capitals only)
both tables are drawn, each under its own caption
each table names its source
each pie part is listed with its amount and its share
the whole is shown in the centre of the ring (₹20,995.3)
a bare amount in a table gets the Indian grouping, with the decimals as printed
a whole amount is grouped too, a small one is untouched
a year is not an amount (2024 stays 2024)
a rupee sign is kept
a date and a text cell are not touched
an amount written '₹ 2400/-' is grouped and keeps its '/-'
DA is explained, and 'IITs' / 'IIMs' are the abbreviations IIT / IIM
an abbreviation the circular defines itself (FA) is explained, from the circular's own words
an empty condition [] is never drawn
a chart with paise shows two decimals everywhere, one without keeps whole numbers
the ring's list prints paise the same way for every part (₹1,720.30, ₹52.00, ₹3,350.00) and the total with two decimals
shares always have one decimal (17.9%... not 18%)
